MILAB and Marabac had traded their store of uncut jewels, of carven talismans and small jasper and carnelian idols, making a good profit in Faraad. Now, laden with rosy and purple-black pearls from the southern gulfs, and the black sapphires and winy garnets of Yoros, they were returning northward toward Tasuun with a company of other merchants on the long, circuitous journey to Ustaim by the orient sea

representative.text: I, Udolfo Pordenone, have promised you! And then-ah, then, we shall see!" One, peering inward at that curious chamber, would see, but he would not have believed. For, indeed, as might be seen in any hot-house, there were foxglove, starwort, narcissus, orchis, crane-fly and cipripedium-but hideous, distorted, monstrous beyond all imagining, thrusting aloft with filaments that had grown to cables, stamens that were like writhing columns, pistils that were like gigantic swords. The thing that had become a bayonet was fantastic and dangerous enough, but it was before a curious monster that seemed a cuttlefish rooted in black loam that the professor paused and gloated. Beneath its soaring antennæ, quivering like the sentient fingers of a giant squid, there was a flat, white disk, a dead white, like the belly of a snake

THIS unusual story by the author of "Golden Blood" is replete with thrills and chills. It rises to a climax of blood-curdling horror, and will hold you spellbound with its gripping fascination. The amazing ambition of one who called himself the Wizard of Life, and who moved with sure, confident steps to make himself sole ruler of the world, are pictured by an author who in a few short years has become one of the titans of science-fiction. This astounding weird novelette will be published complete stuff. May I have my say
